title: Chicken 65 / Gobi 65
description: Spicy yoghurt-marinated chicken, or cauliflower for Gobi 65 like from Saravana Bhavan, crisped in the air fryer. Four portions to have with dal, add to fried rice or serve beside a curry.
imageAlt: Crisp rust-red Chicken 65 pieces with curry leaves in a brushed-steel serving dish.
personalNote: Mix the marinade straight in a Tupperware so we don’t have another bowl to wash. Give it at least an hour in the fridge, but a few hours or overnight is much better if we’ve got time.
servingSuggestion: Four portions of Chicken 65 or Gobi 65. Serve with dal, add to fried rice or have as an extra side with a curry. For the cauliflower version, use the cooked florets instead of chicken in the linked fried-rice recipe.
equipment: Tupperware with a lid, large enough for the chicken
advancePrep: Defrost the 4 ginger-garlic cubes so they become a paste. Plan for at least 1 hour of fridge time after coating the chicken; a few hours or overnight is better.
importantNotes: Taste and adjust the seasoned yoghurt mixture before adding the flours. For the chicken version, do the taste test before the raw chicken goes in too. Air fry in a single layer at 200°C, turning and gently shaking halfway, then shaking at the end. Chicken gets 30 minutes per batch; check cauliflower earlier and stop when tender inside and crisp outside. Use both baskets or extra batches if needed.
portionNote: The full batch uses 1 kg chicken breast, or 1 kg cauliflower florets for Gobi 65, and makes 4 portions. Choose the version below so the ingredients and steps match.
choiceIntro: Choose chicken or the cauliflower version, like from Saravana Bhavan. The ingredients and cooking steps follow the choice.

recipeOptions.label: Chicken 65
recipeOptions.description: 1 kg chicken breast for 4 portions, air fried at 200°C for 30 minutes per batch.

ingredients.name: Ginger-garlic cubes
ingredients.note: Defrost fully so they become a paste.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.note: Taste the marinade before the flour and raw chicken go in; adjust if needed.

ingredients.name: Plain yoghurt
ingredients.note: Keep a tiny bit extra handy if the coating is too thick.

ingredients.name: Oil spray
ingredients.note: Spray the bottom of the baskets and the tops of the chicken pieces.

afterSteps.title: Make the seasoned yoghurt straight in the Tupperware
afterSteps.description: Use a clean Tupperware instead of a bowl. Mix the defrosted ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala, black pepper, salt, yoghurt, lime juice and curry leaves together.

afterSteps.title: Taste it before the flour or chicken goes in
afterSteps.description: Give this mixture a taste now and adjust the salt and spices if needed. It should taste really salty and spicy — that will mellow out once it coats all the chicken. Do this taste test before adding the flours or raw chicken.

afterSteps.title: Mix in the two flours
afterSteps.description: Add the cornflour and rice flour or ground rice. Mix them through the marinade until it’s all combined.

afterSteps.title: Cube the chicken and coat it properly
afterSteps.description: Chop the chicken breast into similar-sized cubes and add it to the Tupperware. Mix it around until all the pieces are coated. If the mixture is too thick to coat them, add a tiny bit more yoghurt and mix again.
afterSteps.tip: Similar-sized pieces will cook more evenly. Don’t taste the marinade after the raw chicken has gone in.

afterSteps.title: Lid on and into the fridge
afterSteps.description: Put the lid on and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour. A few hours or overnight is much better if we’ve planned ahead.
afterSteps.tip: The one-hour timer is the minimum marination time. Leave it longer in the fridge if we’ve got time.

afterSteps.title: Oil the baskets and leave the chicken in one layer
afterSteps.description: Spray the bottom of the air fryer baskets with oil. Lay the chicken pieces out in a single layer, then spray the tops with oil too. Use both baskets or cook in batches if we need more space; the pieces need room to crisp.

afterSteps.title: Air fry the first 15 minutes
afterSteps.description: Put the chicken into the air fryer at 200°C and cook for the first 15 minutes.

afterSteps.title: Halfway: flip and shake
afterSteps.description: Flip the chicken pieces with tongs and give the baskets a shake so the pieces move around and crisp on the other sides.

afterSteps.title: Another 15 minutes at 200°C
afterSteps.description: Return the baskets to the air fryer and cook for another 15 minutes at 200°C. That makes 30 minutes of cooking altogether for this batch.

afterSteps.title: One last shake, then check the middle
afterSteps.description: Give the baskets another shake at the end. Check a few of the thickest chicken pieces are fully cooked through before serving. We want crisp edges and hot, cooked chicken inside. If any pieces need more time, put them back in and check again.
afterSteps.doneness: Crisp coating and chicken that is steaming hot through the middle. A clean food thermometer in a thick piece should read at least 75°C.

afterSteps.title: With dal, in fried rice or beside a curry
afterSteps.description: This makes 4 portions. Serve with dal to make a complete meal, add the cooked pieces to fried rice or have them as an extra side with a curry. The dal and the cooked-chicken fried rice recipes are linked below.

recipeOptions.label: Gobi 65 · cauliflower
recipeOptions.description: Swap the chicken for 1 kg cauliflower florets, using the same marinade. Four portions of Gobi 65, like from Saravana Bhavan.

ingredients.name: Ginger-garlic cubes
ingredients.note: Defrost fully so they become a paste.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.note: Taste the marinade before the flour and raw chicken go in; adjust if needed.

ingredients.name: Plain yoghurt
ingredients.note: Keep a tiny bit extra handy if the coating is too thick.

ingredients.name: Cauliflower florets
ingredients.note: Use 1 kg cauliflower florets in place of the chicken. Keep the florets similar sizes.

ingredients.name: Oil spray
ingredients.note: Spray the bottom of the baskets and the tops of the chicken pieces.

afterSteps.title: Make the seasoned yoghurt straight in the Tupperware
afterSteps.description: Use a clean Tupperware instead of a bowl. Mix the defrosted ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala, black pepper, salt, yoghurt, lime juice and curry leaves together.

afterSteps.title: Taste it before the flour goes in
afterSteps.description: Give the seasoned yoghurt mixture a taste now and adjust the salt and spices if needed. It should taste really salty and spicy; that mellows once it coats the cauliflower. Taste before adding the flours.

afterSteps.title: Mix in the two flours
afterSteps.description: Add the cornflour and rice flour or ground rice. Mix them through the marinade until it’s all combined.

afterSteps.title: Break the cauliflower into florets and coat it
afterSteps.description: Use 1 kg of cauliflower florets in place of the chicken. Keep the florets similar sizes and mix them into the marinade until coated. Add a tiny bit more yoghurt if the mixture is too thick.
afterSteps.tip: Keep the florets similar sizes so they cook evenly.

afterSteps.title: Lid on and into the fridge
afterSteps.description: Put the lid on and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour. A few hours or overnight is much better if we’ve planned ahead.
afterSteps.tip: The one-hour timer is the minimum marination time. Leave it longer in the fridge if we’ve got time.

afterSteps.title: Oil the baskets and leave the florets in one layer
afterSteps.description: Spray the bottom of the air fryer baskets with oil. Lay the cauliflower florets out in a single layer, then spray the tops with oil too. Use both baskets or cook in batches if we need more space; the pieces need room to crisp.

afterSteps.title: Air fry the first 15 minutes
afterSteps.description: Put the cauliflower into the air fryer at 200°C and cook for the first 15 minutes.

afterSteps.title: Halfway: flip and shake
afterSteps.description: Turn the florets gently with tongs and give the baskets a gentle shake so the other sides can crisp.

afterSteps.title: Another 15 minutes at 200°C
afterSteps.description: Return the baskets to the air fryer at 200°C for up to another 15 minutes. Check earlier if the florets are small, and stop once they are tender inside with crisp edges. The full 30 minutes is a guide for the cauliflower.

afterSteps.title: One last gentle shake, then check the florets
afterSteps.description: Give the baskets a gentle shake at the end. Check a thick floret with a fork: it should be tender in the middle with crisp edges. Give any firm pieces a little longer if needed.
afterSteps.doneness: Tender cauliflower through the middle, with a crisp, spicy coating.

afterSteps.title: With dal, in fried rice or beside a curry
afterSteps.description: This makes 4 portions of Gobi 65, like the cauliflower version from Saravana Bhavan. Serve with dal or rice, or as an extra side with a curry. For fried rice, use these cooked florets in place of the chicken in the linked fried-rice recipe.

substitutions.title: Rice flour or ground rice
substitutions.text: Use 1 tablespoon of either, along with the 2 tablespoons of cornflour.

substitutions.title: The coating is too thick
substitutions.text: Add a tiny bit of extra yoghurt and mix it through so the marinade coats all the chicken.

substitutions.title: Make it a meal
substitutions.text: Serve Chicken 65 with the dal for a complete meal. It also works mixed into fried rice, or as an extra side with a curry.

substitutions.title: Gobi 65, like from Saravana Bhavan
substitutions.text: Choose the Gobi 65 tab and swap the chicken for the same weight of cauliflower florets. Use the same marinade, keep the florets similar sizes and check for a tender middle and crisp edges. Small florets may cook sooner than the chicken.

troubleshooting.title: The coating isn’t crisp enough
troubleshooting.text: Leave space between the pieces, spray the tops with oil and remember the halfway flip and shake, plus another shake at the end. Use extra batches if needed instead of stacking the pieces.

troubleshooting.title: One batch won’t fit
troubleshooting.text: Use both baskets or cook in separate single-layer batches. The 30-minute cooking time is for each batch; allow more time if cooking batches one after another.

storage: Marinate in the covered Tupperware in the fridge. If preparing ahead, a few hours or overnight is better. Cool cooked leftovers quickly and refrigerate within 1–2 hours; use within 2 days.
reheating: Reheat only the portion we’re eating, once, until steaming hot throughout. If adding saved Chicken 65 or Gobi 65 to fried rice, heat the pieces through fully with the rice.
foodSafety: Taste the seasoned yoghurt before adding the flours or raw chicken. For Chicken 65, check the thickest pieces reach at least 75°C before serving. For Gobi 65, cook until the florets are tender through the middle.
